opening.text: Imagine that every morning someone hands you an envelope. Inside is the same amount of money, every day. You cannot save it for tomorrow. You cannot borrow from the next day. What is not spent by midnight is gone.
That is how time works. Everyone gets the same envelope. What matters is how we spend it.

mainMessage.text: Each day is a gift from God, and we will account for how we use it. The best use of time starts with the right priorities. A short prayer and a few scripture verses in the morning can set the course for the day.

blocks.text: **The envelope is a gift.** We did not earn today. It was given to us. Each day is a chance to prepare and to serve.
For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
This day is a precious gift of God.
Today is a gift.
**Someone will ask.** A good steward knows he will give an account. God asks us to use His gifts well, and time is one of them.
His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The God who gives us each day as a treasure will require an accounting.
We will give an account.
**Spend on what matters most.** When we know what matters most, spending is easy. Our priorities decide what we look for and what we find.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities determine what we seek in life.
Priorities decide what we seek.
**No refunds.** Money not spent wisely can sometimes be earned back. Time cannot. Once an hour is gone, it is gone.
See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We cannot recycle or save the time allotted to us each day.
Time cannot be saved.
**Look at the receipts.** If you want to know your priorities, look at where your hours went. Our time shows what we truly value.
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities are most visible in how we use our time.
Our time shows what we love.
**Spend the first coin well.** The first minutes of the day set the tone. A morning prayer and a short search in the scriptures can point the whole day in the right direction.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
A morning prayer and an early search in the scriptures to know what we should do for the Lord can set the course of a day.
The first minutes set the day.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they used a day well, or wished they had. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nehemiah and the Wall

blocks.text: Nehemiah and the people of Jerusalem had a wall to rebuild, and not much time. They worked together, day after day.
So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.
They did not wait for a perfect day. They used the days they had.

application.text: First, write down your three most important priorities. Then look at your last week. How much time went to each?
Second, move one small block of time, even fifteen minutes, from something less important to something more important.
Third, if you feel you cannot find time for what matters, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that time is a gift from God. I know that He helps us use it well when we ask Him. I have felt peace when I spent a day on what mattered most. I know that Jesus Christ gave His life for us, and that He invites us to follow Him each day. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to write down your three most important priorities and look at how last week matched them.
I invite you to move one small block of time, even fifteen minutes, to something more important.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president if you cannot find time for what matters.
blessings: You will have time for what matters most.

closingVerse.text: And now, as I said unto you before, as ye have had so many witnesses, therefore, I beseech of you that ye do not procrastinate the day of your repentance until the end; for after this day of life, which is given us to prepare for eternity, behold, if we do not improve our time while in this life, then cometh the night of darkness wherein there can be no labor performed.

opening.text: Before a long trip, you pack a backpack. There is only so much room. You cannot take everything. So you choose. You take what you will need and you leave the rest at home.
Each day is like that backpack. There are only so many hours. We cannot fit everything. We have to choose.

mainMessage.text: We cannot do it all, and we were never meant to. When we pack our days with what matters most, we carry less stress and more joy. God helps us decide what goes in.

blocks.text: **The backpack was given.** Someone handed us this day. It is a gift, and it came with purpose.
For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
This day is a precious gift of God.
The day is a gift.
**Someone checks the pack.** At the end of the trip, we report on how it went. God will ask how we used what He gave us, including our days.
His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The God who gives us each day as a treasure will require an accounting.
We will report on the trip.
**Pack by purpose.** A good packer asks what the trip is for. When we know our purpose, it is easier to choose what to carry. Priorities shape what we look for.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities determine what we seek in life.
Purpose decides what we pack.
**You cannot unpack the past.** Once the day is packed and the trip is over, we cannot go back and repack. Time cannot be recycled or saved.
See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We cannot recycle or save the time allotted to us each day.
We cannot repack yesterday.
**Open the pack and look.** What is inside shows what we value. Our priorities are easiest to see in how we use our time.
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities are most visible in how we use our time.
The pack shows what we value.
**Pack first thing.** The best time to pack is the start of the day. A prayer and a few minutes in the scriptures help us pack what the Lord knows we need.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
A morning prayer and an early search in the scriptures to know what we should do for the Lord can set the course of a day.
Morning is the time to pack.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they chose to leave something out so they could make room for something better. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jesus Is About His Father’s Business

blocks.text: At twelve, Jesus stayed behind in the temple. When His parents found Him, He explained what He was doing.
And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?
Even as a boy, Jesus knew His priority. He put it first.

application.text: First, list everything you plan to do tomorrow. Circle the three that matter most.
Third, if your list feels too heavy, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God cares how we spend our days. I know that He gives peace to those who put Him first. I have felt less pressure when I chose what mattered most. I know that Jesus Christ shows us how to use our time. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to list what you plan to do tomorrow and circle the three that matter most.
I invite you to do those three first.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president if your list feels too heavy.

closingVerse.text: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.

opening.text: Stand at the edge of a river and watch the water go by. You cannot scoop up the same water twice. What passed a minute ago is already far downstream. All you can do is decide what to do with the water in front of you right now.
Time flows like that. It does not wait. What we do with it, we do now.

mainMessage.text: Time keeps moving, and every day is a gift from God. We cannot hold it back or call it back. But we can use it well by choosing what matters most and asking the Lord to guide us.

blocks.text: **The river is a gift.** The river flows because someone made it. Our days are given to us by God, and they are a treasure.
For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
This day is a precious gift of God.
The river is a gift.
**The river has an owner.** The river belongs to the One who made it. He asks us to use what He gives us wisely. One day we will report on it.
His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The God who gives us each day as a treasure will require an accounting.
We will give an account.
**Choose where to fish.** You cannot fish the whole river. You choose a place. When we know what matters most, we know where to cast. Our priorities decide what we seek.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities determine what we seek in life.
Priorities decide where we cast.
**You cannot bottle the river.** You can fill a cup, but the river keeps going. Time cannot be saved up for later. We can only spend it.
See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We cannot recycle or save the time allotted to us each day.
Time cannot be bottled.
**Watch where the water goes.** If a river is turned into a channel, you can see where it was sent. Our days work the same way. Where our time goes shows what we value.
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities are most visible in how we use our time.
We can see where it goes.
**Start at the spring.** The source of a river is up in the hills. For a day, the source is the morning. A prayer and a few scriptures at the start can shape the whole stream.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
A morning prayer and an early search in the scriptures to know what we should do for the Lord can set the course of a day.
The morning shapes the stream.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when starting the day with the Lord changed how it went. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jesus Prays Early

blocks.text: Jesus had a full schedule. People wanted His time all day. But He made room to be alone with His Father.
And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
If the Savior made time for prayer, we can too.

application.text: First, set your alarm ten minutes earlier tomorrow.
Second, use those ten minutes for a prayer and a few verses of scripture.
Third, if your schedule feels too full to find even ten minutes, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the Lord helps us shape our days. I know that early prayer brings peace. I have felt Him guide my hours when I asked. I know that Jesus Christ made time for His Father, and that He invites us to do the same. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to set your alarm ten minutes earlier tomorrow.
I invite you to use those ten minutes for a prayer and a few verses of scripture.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president if your schedule feels too full.
blessings: You will begin the day with the Spirit.
You will find time for the best things.

closingVerse.text: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.

opening.text: A farmer is up before the sun. The cows need milking. The fields need checking. If he waits until noon, the best part of the day is already gone. He does what matters most first, and the rest of the day goes more smoothly.
There is wisdom in that. How we begin the day shapes how it goes.

mainMessage.text: A good day starts with a good beginning. We use our time best when we know what matters most, start with the Lord and then do the work in front of us.

blocks.text: **The morning is a gift.** The farmer does not make the sunrise. He receives it. Each day is given to us by God.
For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
This day is a precious gift of God.
The morning is given.
**The harvest is counted.** At the end of the season, the farmer counts what he brought in. We will also give an account of how we used our days.
His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The God who gives us each day as a treasure will require an accounting.
The harvest is counted.
**First the cows, then the rest.** A farmer knows what cannot wait. Our priorities tell us what comes first. They decide what we look for in life.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities determine what we seek in life.
Priorities say what comes first.
**You cannot plant last season.** Once the season is gone, it is gone. We cannot go back and plant again. Time cannot be saved or recycled.
See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We cannot recycle or save the time allotted to us each day.
The season does not come back.
**The fields tell the story.** You can tell what a farmer cares about by looking at his fields. A calendar tells the same story about us. Our priorities show in how we use our time.
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities are most visible in how we use our time.
The fields tell the story.
**Before the first chore.** A wise farmer starts with a look at the sky. A wise disciple starts with prayer and the scriptures. They help us know what the Lord wants done today.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
A morning prayer and an early search in the scriptures to know what we should do for the Lord can set the course of a day.
We look to the sky first.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they put first things first and it made a difference. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nephi Is Told to Build a Ship

blocks.text: Nephi was given a big task. He did not know how to build a ship. But he went to work, one step at a time, as the Lord showed him.
And it came to pass that the Lord spake unto me, saying: Thou shalt construct a ship, after the manner which I shall show thee, that I may carry thy people across these waters.
Nephi used his days on what the Lord asked, and the ship was built.

application.text: First, ask in prayer, “What should I do first today?”
Second, do that one thing before anything else.
Third, if you feel overwhelmed by what is on your plate, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the Lord knows what our days need. I know that He guides those who ask. I have felt Him direct my steps, one at a time. I know that Jesus Christ is the Lord of every good work. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to ask in prayer, "What should I do first today?"
I invite you to do that one thing before anything else.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president if you feel overwhelmed.
blessings: You will use your day well.

closingVerse.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

opening.text: A train does not wait for late passengers. It leaves on time. If you run to the platform and the doors are closed, you wait for the next one. But if you know the timetable and plan for it, you are on board with time to spare.
Our days run on a kind of timetable too. They keep moving. The wise plan ahead.

mainMessage.text: We are given a day at a time, and each one counts. Knowing what matters most helps us plan well. Starting the day with the Lord helps us stay on the right line.

blocks.text: **A ticket we did not buy.** We were handed this day. It is a gift, and a precious one.
For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
This day is a precious gift of God.
The ticket is a gift.
**The conductor will ask.** At the end of the journey, there is an accounting. God will ask how we used the days He gave us.
His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
The God who gives us each day as a treasure will require an accounting.
We will give an account.
**Know your destination.** You cannot plan a trip without knowing where you are going. Our priorities decide what we seek in life.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities determine what we seek in life.
The destination sets the route.
**The train will not come back.** If you miss it, it is gone. The hours we have today cannot be saved or recycled. We use them or lose them.
See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We cannot recycle or save the time allotted to us each day.
The hours do not come back.
**The timetable shows what we care about.** If you want to know where someone is going, look at their timetable. Our time shows what we truly value.
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Focus and Priorities” from the April 2001 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Our priorities are most visible in how we use our time.
Our time shows our priorities.
**Check the board first.** A good traveler checks the departures board first thing. A faithful disciple checks in with the Lord first thing. A morning prayer and scripture time set the course.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder Henry B. Eyring, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “This Day” from the April 2007 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
A morning prayer and an early search in the scriptures to know what we should do for the Lord can set the course of a day.
We check with the Lord first.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they gave what they had, even when it was small, and it counted. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The Widow Gives All She Has

blocks.text: A poor widow put two small coins into the treasury. It was not much. But Jesus saw it differently.

And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.
What we give matters more than how much we give. Even a small amount of time, given with love, is large to the Lord.

application.text: First, pick one person you want to give time to this week. Set a specific time and put it on your calendar.
Second, keep that appointment, even if it is short.
Third, if you feel pulled in too many directions, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that every day is a gift from God. I know that He sees how we use even the small moments. I have felt joy when I gave my time to what mattered. I know that Jesus Christ gave His whole life for us. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to pick one person to give time to this week and put it on your calendar.
I invite you to keep that appointment, even if it is short.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president if you feel pulled in too many directions.

closingVerse.text: And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
